newsitem.title: USA: U.S lawmaker to offer bill on stock decimalization.
newsitem.headline: U.S lawmaker to offer bill on stock decimalization.

text.p: Rep. Rick Lazio, a New York Republican, plans to introduce legislation in the coming weeks that would stall Congressional efforts to move stock quoting in the United States to dollars and cents from fractions, an aide said Friday.
"We are drafting a bill and we are actively seeking co- sponsors," the aide said.

Lazio's measure would require an investigation before the House Commerce Committee can act on separate bi-partisan legislation that was introduced in March that calls on the SEC to develop a plan within year to transition stock and options markets away from trading in fractions.
Lazio's bill would require "a thorough study of the issue," the aide said. "We don't think that's been done and hopefully we will have language in the hopper."
Earlier this month, the Commerce Committee's subcommittee on Finance and Hazardous Materials heard testimony from both supporters and those opposed to the decimalization measure.

Such a shift would enable investors to save money in transactions costs because there would be a narrow difference between the prices at which they buy and sell stocks, supporters of the legislation said.

Others, including the subcommittee's ranking minority member Thomas Manton, a New York Democrat, echoed the concerns raised by securities industry officials, warning that such a move could be disruptive and is a decision to be made by the markets rather than by Congress.
